tier1.text: Each gracilis pulls the thigh in toward the body, a movement called adduction. The strap-like gracilis also flexes, or bends, the knee. The gracilis runs straight down the inner thigh, nearer the surface than any other muscle there.

sentences.text: Each gracilis pulls the thigh in toward the body, a movement called adduction.

quotes.quote: gracilis: muscle that adducts the thigh and flexes the leg at the knee
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: adduction is the opposing movement that brings the limb toward the body or across the midline
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The strap-like gracilis also flexes, or bends, the knee.

quotes.quote: Along with the adductor longus, adductor brevis, adductor magnus, and pectineus, the strap-like gracilis adducts the thigh in addition to flexing the leg at the knee.

quotes.quote: flexion: movement in the sagittal plane that decreases the angle of a joint (bends the joint)
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: The most superficial muscle extending vertically downward along the inner thigh which adducts the thigh, rotates the leg medially and flexes the knee.
quotes.citation: NCI Thesaurus (NCIt), National Cancer Institute, https://ncithesaurus.nci.nih.gov
